DA-P0-010.description: correctness cache identity uses strict + >=128 bit
implementation: Added hash_correctness_identity() function with strict=True and 256-bit default
IdentityDigest type='correctness' enforces minimum 128 bits
Separate from hash_cache_key() for ephemeral performance cache (64-bit allowed)
Documentation clarifies use case: cache affecting quantitative result correctness
Strict mode raises ValidationError for unknown object types
Error message enhanced: 'DA-P0-011: Cannot encode {type} in strict mode. Correctness identity禁止repr fallback.'
Lists all supported types: None, bool, int, float, str, bytes, datetime, Enum, list, tuple, set, frozenset, dict, dataclass
Non-strict mode preserves backward compatibility with repr fallback
Set encoding preserves element type: (type_tag, encoded_value) pairs
Deterministic ordering via JSON-encoded tuple sorting
Prevents collision: {1, 2, 3} != {'1', '2', '3'}
Mixed-type sets maintain full type information
Dict key encoding preserves type: ((key_type, encoded_key), encoded_value)
Deterministic key ordering via canonical representation sorting
Prevents collision: {1: 'a'} != {'1': 'a'}
Mixed-type dict keys maintain type distinction
NaN: {'__float_special__': 'NaN'} - stable identity across all NaN bit patterns
+Inf: {'__float_special__': '+Inf'}
-Inf: {'__float_special__': '-Inf'}
-0.0: {'__float_special__': '-0.0'} - detected via math.copysign
+0.0: encoded as literal 0.0
Regular floats: {'__float__': value} - exact representation preserved

hash_correctness_identity.purpose: Hash correctness cache identity with strict encoding and minimum 128 bits
hash_correctness_identity.use_case: Cache that affects quantitative result correctness (factor computation, data transformation feeding into factors)
guarantees: strict=True: no repr fallback, fail-closed on unknown types
type-preserving for sets and dict keys

backward_compatibility.hash_cache_key: PRESERVED - still supports 64-bit for ephemeral performance cache
backward_compatibility.non_strict_mode: PRESERVED - backward compatible repr fallback for legacy code

semantic_guarantees.type_safety: int and str with same numeric value produce different identities

float_semantics.nan_stability: All NaN bit patterns collapse to single identity token
float_semantics.regular_floats: Exact representation preserved, no precision loss
